title: Lean redesign of gastroenterology referral triage with a structured referral template: an improvement report from a regional central intake
abstract: Problem: 22 percent of gastroenterology referrals to a regional central intake were returned for missing information and the median time to triage was nine working days. Intervention: lean redesign of intake rework, then a structured referral template with a documented test exception. Measures: weekly returned referrals, time to triage, template bypass and practice completion time. Results and conclusions will be written after June 2027.
introduction: Structured referral forms improve completeness, but evidence on triage time conflicts and practice workload is rarely measured. No evaluation of a template introduced within a lean redesign of a central intake was found.
methods: Value stream mapping and A3 cycles from January 2027 after a twelve-week baseline; countermeasures introduced in sequence; p-chart and run charts with rules fixed in advance; SQUIRE 2.0 reporting.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the value stream map, the charts with dated countermeasures, bypass, practice timing and returned referrals by practice group.
discussion: The discussion will interpret any change against the conflicting published results on triage time and state whether the template or the intake redesign accounts for it.
limitations: One intake; overlapping countermeasures; small practice timing sample; aggregate data only.
conclusion: To be written after June 2027; it will be limited to this intake and will not claim that templates shorten triage time in general.
summary: SQUIRE-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
